step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes the Amazie.io Lagoon platform. It starts with developers pushing code to a Git repository, which triggers webhooks to the core Lagoon platform, running on an EKS cluster. Lagoon then orchestrates the deployment of developer environments on a separate EKS cluster. This developer EKS cluster utilizes both standard EC2 instances for base workloads and EC2 Spot instances for cost-effective development and non-production environments. For data persistence and storage, the EKS cluster, through an operator, provisions Aurora databases (specifically using Graviton2 R6G instances), EBS volumes (utilizing GP3 for better performance and cost), and EFS for general file storage.

graph.name: Amazie.io Lagoon Platform Architecture
graph.notes: This architecture illustrates Amazie.io's Lagoon platform, an open-source application delivery platform, leveraging AWS EKS for both its core and developer environments. It highlights the use of EC2, EC2 Spot, Aurora (R6G), EBS (GP3), and EFS for compute and storage needs.

nodes.name: GIT
nodes.notes: Git repositories where developers push their code. Webhooks are configured to trigger Lagoon.

nodes.name: LAGOOON EKS
nodes.notes: The EKS cluster running the core Lagoon open source application delivery platform.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: The EKS cluster providing environments for developers, managed by Lagoon.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Standard EC2 instances used by the EKS developer environments for base infrastructure and general workloads.

nodes.name: EC2 SPOT
nodes.notes: EC2 Spot instances used by the EKS developer environments for development and non-productive infrastructure to achieve cost savings of 70-90%.

nodes.name: AURORA R6G
nodes.notes: Aurora database provisioned by Lagoon's EKS operator for developer environments, utilizing Graviton2 (R6G) instances for improved performance and cost-efficiency.

nodes.name: EBS GP3
nodes.notes: EBS volumes provisioned by Lagoon's EKS operator for specialized workloads like databases or search servers, leveraging GP3 volumes for lower storage costs and better IOPS performance.

nodes.name: EFS
nodes.notes: EFS file system provisioned by Lagoon's EKS operator for general asset storage and files that don't need anything specific.

edges.notes: Developers create code and push it to their Git repositories.
Git repository webhooks are connected to Lagoon, triggering the platform on code pushes.
Lagoon processes the Git events and orchestrates the deployment of environments to the developer-facing EKS cluster.
The EKS cluster utilizes standard EC2 instances for its base infrastructure and workloads.
The EKS cluster leverages EC2 Spot instances for development and non-productive infrastructure where failures can be tolerated, reducing costs.
An operator within the EKS cluster provisions Aurora databases as requested by developer deployments, exposing them as secrets.
An operator within the EKS cluster provisions EBS volumes for specialized workloads requiring dedicated block storage.
An operator within the EKS cluster provisions EFS file systems for general, scalable file storage for applications.
